text: This snowboarder just cracked the slope, and the whole mountain is coming down.
Nine in ten victims trigger the slide themselves, and it can hit eighty miles an hour in five seconds.
His best move is to ride hard to the side, off the moving slab.
Too late. It grabs him, so he swims hard to stay near the top.
As it slows down, he punches one hand toward the sky,
and cups his other arm over his face to make an air pocket.
Because the second it stops, the snow sets up like concrete.
Spitting to find which way is up? Avalanche experts call that a myth. He can't dig out anyway.
His life is in his friends' hands now. Dug out within fifteen minutes, ninety-three percent survive.
And that's how you survive an avalanche.
